answer: No, your records show no blood clot in your lungs. You had a CT scan of your chest with contrast on 8 July 2025, which was done to check for a pulmonary embolism (a clot in the lung). The report says there was no pulmonary embolism, and your lungs were clear. A blood test taken the same day, a D-dimer, was raised. That test is sensitive but not specific, so a raised result often prompts a scan like this one. The scan did not find a clot, and the clot diagnosis was ruled out. The same date is recorded as chest wall pain, which resolved by 22 July 2025. Your records show no later clot diagnosis and no blood thinner medicine. If you still have symptoms such as sudden breathlessness, chest pain or coughing blood, please contact your doctor or get urgent care.
short: The 8 July 2025 CT angiography of the chest showed no pulmonary embolism and clear lungs. The pulmonary embolism diagnosis was ruled out, and the chest pain was recorded as chest wall pain that resolved.

knowledge.says: A CT pulmonary angiogram is the standard scan for diagnosing a pulmonary embolism; a negative scan rules it out.
knowledge.guideline: ACR Appropriateness Criteria and ESC guidance on acute pulmonary embolism diagnosis.

items.why: A raised D-dimer prompts imaging to check for a clot, but it does not on its own mean a clot is present.

facts.says: The D-dimer result from 8 July 2025 was 0.92 mg/L FEU, flagged high against a reference of 0.49 or below.

knowledge.says: D-dimer has high sensitivity but low specificity, so a raised level is common with many conditions and is followed by imaging.
knowledge.guideline: NICE NG158 and ESC pulmonary embolism guidance on D-dimer use.
